chapter: Teddy Wilson, Cafe Society and bebop
title: Billie Holiday, frightening at first and lovable at Cafe Society
summary: He feared her cursing at Kelly's Stables but found her sweet and lovable at Cafe Society.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Well, Billie, I'll tell you the truth, when I first met Billie I was very much frightened of her. Cause I heard so many things about how she'd curse out the
musicians, she'd walk out there and call you all kinds of dirty names.
You know, and I was very -- I was frightened of Billie when I first work -- first time I worked with Billie was at Kelly's Stables.

You know, little odd gigs that I played on 52nd Street. She really turned around -- she was beautiful as far as I was concerned, when you think you was satisfying her and I thought sometimes the band was satisfying her, when she finished she'd turn around and call the band a whole lot of dirty names, and go back and hide in her dressing room. And I never could understand why, I thought the band was satisfying her.
But they say she was like that. But at Cafe Society I found her to be entirely different. I found her to be very lovable person. Oh, as sweet as she could be. Always happy, you know, lovable person.
